newsitem.title: BULGARIA: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES-JUNE 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES-JUNE 9.

text.p: The following stories were reported in this week's Bulgarian business weeklies. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

-- Bulgaria's central bank allowed joint stock companies Bulgaria Holding, Energia Insurance and Bulgaria Insurance and Reinsurance to acquire 80, 10 and 10 percent of the voting shares of the ailing state-owned Yambol bank respectively.

The local holding group will invest 3.8 billion levs in the bank, which has been in receivership since September 23, to raise its capital to 3.813 billion levs and the bank will be renamed to Bulgaria Invest commercial bank following the acquisition.

-- International Monetary Fund mission head Anne McGuirk said the IMF was satisfied with the performance of Bulgaria's new reformist cabinet and its preparations to introduce a restrictive monetary regime known as currency board.

McGuirk said that a second $130 million tranche under a $510 million funding agreement with the IMF would be disbursed next month and a third $86 milion tranche could be expected by the end of the summer if Bulgaria meets projected economic targets.

-- Bulgaria's state-owned Biohim Bank has collected some 11 billion levs of overdue debts between end-March and May 23 to raise liquidity and meet IMF requirements for operations under a currency board system.
-- South Korea's Daewoo Corp. bought 70 percent of the Interpred World Trade Centre in Sofia for $20 million.

The buyer, which is expected to transfer the money up to 30 days after signing the sell-off contract, has pledged to invest $5 million in Interpred over the next five years and to preserve the current number of employees for a year after the sale.
-- Bulgaria's parliament passed amendments to the central bank law to adjust central bank operations to the requirements of a currency board system, to be launched on July 1.
The law also set the mark as anchor in the currency board arrangement at a fixed exchange rate of 1,000 levs, to become effective also on July 1.

-- The Issue Department at the central bank will implement the currency board functions, overseeing that levs in circulation were fully matched by foreign exchange reserves, estimated at around $1 billion at the time of the introduction of the currency board. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 91188
